definition-section.comment:
TEST/STEP DEFINITION blocks hold prose values. Inside them only comments, macros, strings, the 
/
 markup and the field keys are highlighted — numbers, units, operators, literals and constants in descriptions are left as default text.
definition-section.name: meta.definition.esi

comments.comment: A '#' starts a line comment to end-of-line. Listed first so macros/tags inside a comment are not separately highlighted.
comments.name: comment.line.number-sign.esi

markup.comment:
The 
 …
/
markup of multi-line description values. Plain single-line matches, deliberately NOT a begin/end region: an unclosed 
 must never swallow the rest of the file.
markup.name: meta.tag.markup.esi

step-tags.comment: [STEP <id>], [/STEP <id>] and the one-liner [STEP <id>/] — a step itself, as opposed to the fixed STEP DEFINITION / INPUTS / OUTPUTS / DUMP parts of one. Mirrors isStepSectionName() in src/lib/sectionNames.ts.

section-tags.comment: The fixed structural sections. The list mirrors src/lib/sectionNames.ts (a unit test keeps the two in step).

tags.comment: Every other tag — component connections ([429_…], [ED_…], …; re-coloured by the semantic-token provider) and anything unrecognised: [NAME], [/NAME] and the one-liner [NAME/] (opens and closes on one line). The closing slash of either form gets its own scope so the name colours the same in all three forms.

occurrence-operator.comment: The optional '<' / '>' in front of an `occurrence` count (occurrence = >3). Limited to `occurrence`: it is the only key the validator knows to take a comparison operator.

field-keys.comment: Any `key =` left-hand side (section keys like 'Step Description', 'system call', 'result file', 'time', message field names, …). Coloured as a keyword; message field keys inside component blocks are re-coloured (orange) by the semantic-token provider.

csv-cell-refs.comment: The cell address of a CSV value reference: `<file>.csv line:<N> col:<M>` (same shape as parseCsvCellRef in src/lib/fileRefs.ts, case-insensitive). The file itself is coloured by file-paths; this rule starts right after the `.csv`.
csv-cell-refs.name: meta.csv-ref.esi

file-paths.comment: File-path values: a path-like token (folders with / or \ separators, optional drive letter) ending in a short alphabetic extension — e.g. ../../Utilities/DumpReadLog.py, C:\dir\file.csv, report.html, tool.exe. Extension-agnostic (any 1–7 letter extension) so new types like .exe/.html need no list; numeric suffixes (1.5, 192.168.0.1) and N/A are excluded because the extension must start with a letter.
file-paths.name: string.other.path.esi

folder-paths.comment: Directory paths without a file extension — e.g. folder/subfolder, folder\subfolder\, ../../Utilities/, C:\dir\. Same colour as file paths. Requires a separator after a ./ ../ drive, or a 2+ char segment, so values like N/A are not matched.
folder-paths.name: string.other.path.esi

strings.comment: Double-quoted string literals — straight ("…") and typographic/curly (“…”) quotes.
strings.name: string.quoted.double.esi

numbers.comment: Integers, decimals, hex and signed/exponent forms — only as standalone tokens, never inside identifiers like DO-260B_11503.
numbers.name: constant.numeric.esi

numbers-with-unit.comment: A decimal number with a unit suffix glued on (10ms, 2.5s, 400Hz). Purely lexical, from a fixed list of common unit spellings — it says nothing about which units TestPit accepts. Listed after `numbers`, so hex (0x1F) and exponent (1e5) forms are taken there first.
